parameters.content:
## AI Demand Forecasting Workflow

Starter template from agentmelt.com — configure before running:

1. Fill in "Config (edit me)" (name, approver, quiet hours; test_mode stays on for the first week).
2. Add credentials to every service node (Anthropic, mail, CRM, database…).
3. Replace placeholder URLs, queries and field mappings with yours.
4. Set the trigger: Runs Sunday night after the ERP's weekly close. A second, lighter run on Wednesday refreshes the short-term horizon with the latest POS data for the top movers.
5. Keep the gates: 'Needs a person?' after every AI step, 'Approved?' after the approval — wire their dead ends to a sheet or a channel.
6. Keep the guardrails:
   - The model forecasts; the agent explains. No language model touches a number that goes into replenishment.
   - Every run scores the previous run's accuracy so drift is visible within a week.
   - Planner overrides are captured and evaluated against the model, not silently overwritten.
   - Forecasts carry quantiles, and safety stock uses them — a point forecast alone hides the uncertainty that drives stockouts.

Full blueprint and pricing: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/demand-forecasting/
Want it built and run for you? $297/month · custom $5,000–9,000 one-time

nodes.name: Schedule Trigger (weekly)
nodes.notes:
Schedule Trigger (weekly, after the sales data closes)

Runs Sunday night after the ERP's weekly close. A second, lighter run on Wednesday refreshes the short-term horizon with the latest POS data for the top movers.

assignments.name: config.your_name
assignments.value: Your name — signs every outgoing message

assignments.name: config.approver
assignments.value: #approvals — a Slack channel, or an email address

nodes.name: Config (edit me)
nodes.notes:
Fill these in once; every later node reads them as $('Config (edit me)').item.json.config.*

test_mode = true: log what the workflow would write, without writing it, for the first week.
approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

Also point the nodes at your own sources:
- Sales history by SKU-location-week (ERP / data warehouse)
- Promotion and price calendars
- Marketing spend and web analytics
- Weather (Open-Meteo, Visual Crossing) and public holidays
- Stockout / inventory position (to correct censored demand)

nodes.name: Postgres: Pull sales history
nodes.notes:
Pull sales history

Units sold per SKU per location per week from the ERP or data warehouse (NetSuite, SAP, Dynamics, BigQuery, Snowflake), including returns and stockout flags so lost sales are not read as low demand.

parameters.notes: Promotion calendar, price history, marketing spend, web sessions per product, weather for store regions, public holidays, and competitor price feeds where you have them. Each becomes a feature aligned to the same SKU-location-week grid.

nodes.name: HTTP Request: Pull the signals
nodes.notes:
Pull the signals

Promotion calendar, price history, marketing spend, web sessions per product, weather for store regions, public holidays, and competitor price feeds where you have them. Each becomes a feature aligned to the same SKU-location-week grid.

nodes.name: Code: Clean and align
nodes.notes:
Clean and align

Fills gaps, corrects stockout weeks (censored demand), maps promotions to weeks, and produces one wide table per SKU-location. Bad rows are logged, not silently dropped.

parameters.notes: Calls the forecasting service — a gradient-boosted model (LightGBM) or a foundation time-series model (Chronos, TimesFM) hosted as an endpoint, or Nixtla's TimeGPT API for teams that do not want to host. Returns point forecasts and quantiles (p10/p50/p90) for the next 13 weeks.

nodes.name: HTTP Request: Run the forecasting model
nodes.notes:
Run the forecasting model

Calls the forecasting service — a gradient-boosted model (LightGBM) or a foundation time-series model (Chronos, TimesFM) hosted as an endpoint, or Nixtla's TimeGPT API for teams that do not want to host. Returns point forecasts and quantiles (p10/p50/p90) for the next 13 weeks.

nodes.name: Code: Score last week's forecast
nodes.notes:
Score last week's forecast

Compares the forecast made a week ago to the actuals that just arrived and computes WAPE, bias and forecast-value-added by segment, so the workflow reports its own accuracy every run.

nodes.name: Postgres: Write forecasts to the planning system
nodes.notes:
Write forecasts to the planning system

Stores forecasts and quantiles by SKU-location-week, with a run id, in the table the planning tool or replenishment sheet reads.

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Explain the exceptions" step of the AI Demand Forecasting Workflow workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: For SKUs where the forecast moved by more than a threshold or error was worst, the agent reads the feature changes (a new promotion, a price drop, a stockout) and writes a one-line explanation with the numbers. It never changes a forecast.

Rules:
- The model forecasts; the agent explains. No language model touches a number that goes into replenishment.
- Every run scores the previous run's accuracy so drift is visible within a week.
- Planner overrides are captured and evaluated against the model, not silently overwritten.
- Forecasts carry quantiles, and safety stock uses them — a point forecast alone hides the uncertainty that drives stockouts.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.

nodes.name: AI Agent: Explain the exceptions
nodes.notes:
Explain the exceptions

For SKUs where the forecast moved by more than a threshold or error was worst, the agent reads the feature changes (a new promotion, a price drop, a stockout) and writes a one-line explanation with the numbers. It never changes a forecast.

nodes.name: Needs a person?
nodes.notes: True = the AI step was not sure or flagged the item → dead letter, a person looks. False = continue. Wire the dead letter to a Slack message or a sheet so nothing fails silently.

nodes.name: Needs a person: Explain the exceptions
nodes.notes: Dead letter. Replace this no-op with a Slack message or a sheet row that carries the raw item and the reason — silent failures are the ones that cost.

nodes.name: Slack: Publish the weekly review
nodes.notes:
Publish the weekly review

Posts the accuracy scorecard, the top exceptions with explanations, and a link to the planning sheet. Planners override in the sheet; overrides are stored and scored separately so you learn whether they help.
